content.text: This clause meets the preferred position on every material term.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: § 8.2 provides automatic renewal for successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal) with a Customer opt-out on only thirty days' written notice, plus a Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal and an extension of the opt-out deadline if the reminder is not sent. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. This matches the preferred position (≤30-day notice window, 12-month renewal term, 60-day reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%), so no redline is warranted. The three-year initial term in § 8.1 is a negotiated initial commitment, not an auto-renewal term, and is outside this rule.
